messages:
incident-bot: Alert: Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate in prod, p95 1800ms -> 4s, p99 9s, error rate 6% (deploy: release/2026-03-15-09). Graph: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/alert-xyz
sofia (oncall): I'm on it. Which shard/region?
miguel: us-west-2 primary fleet. Logs show gateway timeouts to runtime pool and long queue waits. sample log:
```
2026-03-15T09:10:12Z GET /v1/generate 504 upstream_timeout id=abc123 wait_ms=4200 queue_ms=3500 runtime_err=kv_eviction
```
sofia (oncall): @ajay can you check release diff — any kernel/kvcache changes?
ajay: recent deploy included a runtime change: KV cache padding logic + enabling adaptive batching for some models. Diff snippet: enable_adaptive_batching=true; kv_padding=8
jenna: support is seeing customer errors, CS: "we're getting 504s for our users" — impacted tenants: 4 high-volume customers; estimated 10% of requests failing for them.
sofia (oncall): okay, immediate plan: 1) try a config rollback (disable adaptive batching) on a single AZ 2) if not stable, revert release. @eng-release-bot can we stage a config flip?
eng-release-bot: rolling config override 'adaptive_batching=false' to prod/us-west-2/a ... started
miguel: applying override... hitting 429s from rate-limiter for a shard, not good. Metrics: runtime queue depth unchanged, KV cache hit rate dropped ~30% after deploy.
sofia (oncall): hmm KV cache drop -> more recompute + memory pressure -> stalls. Try reducing max_concurrency on gateway for that route to shed load.
ajay: issuing gateway change: set route /v1/generate max_concurrency=40 (was 200)
sofia (oncall): command: `curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/routes/modify -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","max_concurrency":40}'` -> response: 202 Accepted
support-bot: Notifying affected customers: templates sent to 4 tenants. Ticket IDs: S-3421,S-3422,S-3423,S-3424 
miguel: after concurrency drop p95 down to ~900ms, p99 ~2.1s, errors still ~2.3% — improved but not back to baseline.
sofia (oncall): good. Are we confident config flip will fully stabilize?
jenna: CS needs ETA for full resolution to update customers.
ajay: config flip is temporary mitigation; root cause appears to be KV cache eviction bug introduced by padding change. I'm preparing rollback PR (revert runtime change) — can we do a fast revert?
sofia (oncall): yes. @eng-release-bot execute rollback to release/2026-03-14-stable
eng-release-bot: Starting rollback: revert to release/2026-03-14-stable. Estimated 6 min.
incident-bot: Deploy pipeline started: build#982 revert -> canary -> prod 
sofia (oncall): monitoring canary windows
miguel: canary shows p99 back to ~450ms, errors <0.2% in canary instances
sofia (oncall): promote
eng-release-bot: Promotion completed to prod at 2026-03-15T09:28:22Z
sofia (oncall): Observability: p95 210ms, p99 610ms, error rate 0.2% — rollout successful :white_check_mark: 
jenna: CS update sent: we rolled back the recent runtime change; customers see normal behavior. Apology + postmortem promised.
kai (next-oncall): taking handover at 09:35Z — I'll own the postmortem and ensure regression test for KV padding is added to CI.
sofia (oncall): handing off to @kai. Remaining action items: 1) postmortem with timeline and root cause 2) fix CI regression test for KV eviction/padding 3) add a circuit-breaker to adaptive batching config 4) customer follow-ups
sofia (oncall): closing incident channel, reopen if regressions reappear
incident-bot: Incident resolved: SLA impact mitigated. Incident ID INC-2026-0315-09
